The cert is for type HB-01 with Emax from 10000 to 50000 kg. Should I model this as a model family with models at 10000, ... 50000? The rule says include model_family ONLY if cert covers >1 model variant. Here there's one type designation HB-01 but Emax is a range. Hmm. It could be interpreted as a family of capacities. But the cert only names one type HB-01. I think it's safer to represent Emax as a range at type level: maximum_capacity: value {min: 10000, max: 50000}, unit "kg". Not model matrix since only one model. I'll keep type_level.

The schema's value shape: number | {min,max} | string. A nominal with tolerance — I could express as {min: 693, max: 707} or keep as string "700 ± 7". Rules say don't fabricate but transformation is fine. I think representing nominal with tolerance: maybe value: {min: 693, max: 707}, unit "Ω". But that loses nominal. Alternatively attribute input_impedance value "700 Ω ± 7 Ω"? But unit separation is strict. I'll go with min/max: 693–707 Ω? Hmm, that changes semantics slightly. Alternatively add a second characteristic input_impedance_tolerance: 7 Ω and input_impedance: 700 Ω. That seems cleaner and structured: input_impedance {value: 700, unit "Ω"}, input_impedance_tolerance {value: 7, unit "Ω"}. I'll do that for both input and output impedance.

Actually, better: keep it simple with min/max ranges. The strict shape allows {min,max}. ±7 Ω means range 693–707 Ω. I'll do {min: 693, max: 707} for input impedance and {min: 699, max: 707} for output (703 ± 4). Hmm, 703-4=699, 703+4=707. Yes.

But the nominal info is lost. I could include both nominal and tolerance as separate keys. The schema says characteristics type_level: <label>: {value, unit_symbol, footnote_markers[]}. So each label gets a structured value. I could emit:
- input_impedance_nominal: {value: 700, unit_symbol: "Ω"}
- input_impedance_tolerance: {value: 7, unit_symbol: "Ω"}

That's structured and preserves info. I'll do that.

Actually it says "associated OIML Test Report No. NMi-12200422-01". I'll call it "test_report". Either works; I'll pick "type_evaluation_report" since it's the test report for type evaluation under scheme A. Hmm — the "OIML Test Report" in OIML-CS is the report of the type evaluation. I'll use "type_evaluation_report".

certificate.number: "R60/2017-A-NL1-22.35". Include revision separately? The schema has number, scheme... revision is not in certificate schema, but revision_history exists. model_family: omit since single model? There's only one type HB-01. Emax is a range though. I'll not create model_family. Actually, could argue it covers load cells 10000–50000 kg which are variants. But no explicit model IDs. I'll omit model_family.
